title: The Miraculous Birth of Jesus
subtitle: The virgin birth in the Quran and the Gospels — one miracle, two conclusions
summary: The virgin birth honors Jesus and Mary, but a miraculous origin does not by itself make someone divine. The Quran explains Jesus's birth through God's creative command and compares him with Adam. Christianity joins the birth to a wider case for the incarnation; Islam finds that the miracle is fully explained by an all-powerful Creator sending an extraordinary human Messiah.

seo.metaTitle: The Miraculous Birth of Jesus in the Quran and the Bible
seo.metaDescription: Why Islam affirms Jesus's virgin birth while rejecting divinity: Mary's honor, the comparison with Adam, and the strongest Christian response.
keywords: virgin birth of Jesus in Islam
does Islam believe in the virgin birth

sections.title: A Miraculous Beginning Does Not Decide Who Deserves Worship
sections.body:
Jesus did not need an ordinary conception to be truly human. If God creates every human life, He can create one without a father. The virgin birth therefore gives reason to honor Jesus and Mary, not by itself to worship the child.

Islam and Christianity agree on the miracle but disagree about its meaning. To test the Quran's authority rather than assume it, begin with [Why the Quran?](/articles/why-the-quran).

sections.title: A Rare Point of Deep Agreement
sections.body:
Islam and Christianity share an extraordinary belief: Jesus was conceived by God's direct action without a human father. In both traditions, Mary remains chaste. The Quran and Matthew and Luke state this clearly.

The Quran also honors Mary by name and through Surah Maryam. The central question is what this miracle proves about Jesus.

sections.title: What Follows From a Birth Without a Father?
sections.body:
The Islamic reasoning separates an event from a conclusion about God's identity. A miraculous conception is an extraordinary act of God. It does not follow that the person conceived is God: the Creator can act without becoming the result of His action.

Quran 3:59 makes that distinction through Adam. Within the scriptural account, Adam's creation without either parent is no reason to worship Adam. Jesus's conception without a father cannot, on its own, require worship of Jesus either. This answers an inference from the miracle; it is not a proof that every other Christian argument is false.

sections.title: The Sources and Their Setting
sections.body:
Matthew and Luke contain the New Testament's infancy narratives. They agree that Mary conceived Jesus before living with a husband, though surrounding details differ. The Quran gives its own account in Surahs Al Imran and Maryam, centering Mary's faith and God's command.

Historical method cannot verify a virginal conception directly. The question therefore depends on the reliability of revelation and the meaning each scripture gives the miracle.

sections.title: The Annunciation in the Quran
sections.body:
The angel tells Mary that God gives her "a word from Him" named the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary (Quran 3:45). When she asks how she can have a child, the answer is God's creative command: "When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is" (Quran 3:47).

Surah Maryam repeats this account and calls the birth a sign and mercy (Quran 19:17-21). Afterward, Jesus declares, "I am the servant of Allah ... He has made me a prophet" (Quran 19:30). The Quran joins miracle with servanthood: Jesus is extraordinary because God created him by command, not because God entered creation.

sections.title: The Annunciation in Matthew and Luke
sections.body:
Matthew 1:18-23 and Luke 1 affirm conception by the Holy Spirit before Mary and Joseph came together. Luke calls Jesus Messiah and "Son of the Most High." Christians read these titles through incarnation and divine sonship.

Muslims respect the Gospel witness to Mary's chastity while noting that a miraculous origin alone cannot establish deity. Adam's creation was even more unusual, and Luke calls Adam "son of God" (Luke 3:38) without making him divine.

sections.title: The Stronger Christian Objection
sections.body:
A thoughtful Christian does not usually argue that anyone born without a father must be God. Luke 1:26-35 connects the conception with divine sonship, and Matthew 1:18-23 gives the child the name Immanuel, meaning God with us. Christians read these alongside the wider New Testament account of Jesus.

Islam's answer is not to remove those claims from the discussion. It distinguishes a sign of God's presence and choice from identity with God. The Quran explicitly identifies this miraculously born Messiah as a servant and prophet (19:30). The disagreement must finally be tested through the rival accounts of revelation and of Jesus, not by treating unusual biology as deity.

sections.title: Honor Mary Without Turning the Miracle Into More Than It Shows
sections.body:
The Quran affirms Mary's chastity and calls her chosen (3:42; 21:91). It presents her devotion as an example for believers (66:12). Muslims therefore do not have to give up reverence for Mary or belief in the virgin birth when they reject the incarnation.

Nor does Islam claim that Christian sonship means God physically fathered Jesus. Historic Christian teaching means an eternal relation, not sexual reproduction. Islam rejects that theological claim too, but the Adam comparison addresses the narrower claim that a fatherless birth itself proves it.

sections.title: A Sign of the Creator's Freedom
sections.body:
The Quran's account allows the miracle to remain a miracle. God is not confined to ordinary reproduction; Jesus need not become divine to be born by God's command. This preserves both God's creative freedom and the Messiah's real humanity.

Mary's trust also becomes a practical example. Dependence on God is not a defect that must be escaped by becoming divine. It is the proper relationship of an honored human being to the Creator.

sections.title: Keep the Miracle, Examine the Conclusion
sections.body:
If you love Jesus because of his extraordinary beginning, Islam asks you to keep that love and examine where the sign points. Read Quran 3:42-59 and Luke 1:26-35 in context, distinguishing what each passage says from what is inferred.

Next read [The Miracles of Jesus](/articles/the-miracles-of-jesus). The same question returns there: does God's work through a person make the person God?

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.body:
Q: Do Muslims believe Jesus was born of a virgin?
A: Yes. The Quran states that Mary conceived Jesus while no man had touched her (Quran 3:47; 19:20).

Q: Why is Mary so important in Islam?
A: Mary is the only woman named in the Quran, and Surah 19 bears her name. The Quran says God chose her (Quran 3:42) and presents her as a model of devotion (Quran 66:12).

Q: If Jesus had no father, doesn't that make him the Son of God?
A: A birth without a father does not by itself establish divine sonship: the Quran compares Jesus with Adam (3:59). Christians connect the virgin birth with a wider belief in the eternal Son, not physical fatherhood. Islam affirms the miracle but rejects that further theological conclusion.

Q: Who was the spirit or angel that appeared to Mary?
A: Luke names Gabriel. The Quran calls him 'Our Spirit' (Quran 19:17), and Muslim commentators identify the same messenger.

Q: Do the Quran and the Bible describe the same annunciation?
A: They share the claim of a miraculous conception and honor Mary's chastity, but their narratives and theological meanings are not identical. Matthew and Luke connect Jesus with divine sonship; the Quran presents him as God's created Messiah and servant.

Q: Does the Quran call Jesus the Messiah?
A: Yes. Quran 3:45 calls him 'the Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary.' Islam understands this as a mission, not divinity.

sections.title: Further Reading
sections.body:
Selected sources and further reading:

- **Jesus in the Qur'an**. Geoffrey Parrinder. A respectful survey by a Christian scholar of religion covering the Quranic passages about Jesus and Mary.
- **The Muslim Jesus: Sayings and Stories in Islamic Literature**. Tarif Khalidi. How Jesus is remembered and quoted in the wider Islamic tradition beyond the Quran.
- **The Islamic Jesus**. Mustafa Akyol. An accessible modern discussion of the Quranic Jesus and Mary in conversation with Jewish and Christian views.
- **The Birth of the Messiah**. Raymond E. Brown. A classic Christian scholarly commentary on the infancy narratives of Matthew and Luke.
- **The Qur'an and the Bible: Text and Commentary**. Gabriel Said Reynolds. A verse-by-verse academic comparison of Quranic passages with their biblical parallels, including the Mary narratives.

quranVerses.arabic: وَإِذْ قَالَتِ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ يَٰمَرْيَمُ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱصْطَفَىٰكِ وَطَهَّرَكِ وَٱصْطَفَىٰكِ عَلَىٰ نِسَآءِ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
quranVerses.translation: And [mention] when the angels said, "O Mary, indeed Allah has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: إِذْ قَالَتِ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ يَٰمَرْيَمُ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكِ بِكَلِمَةٍۢ مِّنْهُ ٱسْمُهُ ٱلْمَسِيحُ عِيسَى ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ وَجِيهًۭا فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلْءَاخِرَةِ وَمِنَ ٱلْمُقَرَّبِينَ
quranVerses.translation: [And mention] when the angels said, "O Mary, indeed Allah gives you good tidings of a word from Him, whose name will be the Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary - distinguished in this world and the Hereafter and among those brought near [to Allah].
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: وَيُكَلِّمُ ٱلنَّاسَ فِى ٱلْمَهْدِ وَكَهْلًۭا وَمِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
quranVerses.translation: He will speak to the people in the cradle and in maturity and will be of the righteous."
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: قَالَتْ رَبِّ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لِى وَلَدٌۭ وَلَمْ يَمْسَسْنِى بَشَرٌۭ ۖ قَالَ كَذَٰلِكِ ٱللَّهُ يَخْلُقُ مَا يَشَآءُ ۚ إِذَا قَضَىٰٓ أَمْرًۭا فَإِنَّمَا يَقُولُ لَهُۥ كُن فَيَكُونُ
quranVerses.translation: She said, "My Lord, how will I have a child when no man has touched me?" [The angel] said, "Such is Allah; He creates what He wills. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: وَٱذْكُرْ فِى ٱلْكِتَٰبِ مَرْيَمَ إِذِ ٱنتَبَذَتْ مِنْ أَهْلِهَا مَكَانًۭا شَرْقِيًّۭا
quranVerses.translation: And mention, [O Muhammad], in the Book [the story of] Mary, when she withdrew from her family to a place toward the east.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: فَٱتَّخَذَتْ مِن دُونِهِمْ حِجَابًۭا فَأَرْسَلْنَآ إِلَيْهَا رُوحَنَا فَتَمَثَّلَ لَهَا بَشَرًۭا سَوِيًّۭا
quranVerses.translation: And she took, in seclusion from them, a screen. Then We sent to her Our Angel, and he represented himself to her as a well-proportioned man.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: قَالَتْ إِنِّىٓ أَعُوذُ بِٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ مِنكَ إِن كُنتَ تَقِيًّۭا
quranVerses.translation: She said, "Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, [so leave me], if you should be fearing of Allah."
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: قَالَ إِنَّمَآ أَنَا۠ رَسُولُ رَبِّكِ لِأَهَبَ لَكِ غُلَٰمًۭا زَكِيًّۭا
quranVerses.translation: He said, "I am only the messenger of your Lord to give you [news of] a pure boy."
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: قَالَتْ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لِى غُلَٰمٌۭ وَلَمْ يَمْسَسْنِى بَشَرٌۭ وَلَمْ أَكُ بَغِيًّۭا
quranVerses.translation: She said, "How can I have a boy while no man has touched me and I have not been unchaste?"
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: قَالَ كَذَٰلِكِ قَالَ رَبُّكِ هُوَ عَلَىَّ هَيِّنٌۭ ۖ وَلِنَجْعَلَهُۥٓ ءَايَةًۭ لِّلنَّاسِ وَرَحْمَةًۭ مِّنَّا ۚ وَكَانَ أَمْرًۭا مَّقْضِيًّۭا
quranVerses.translation: He said, "Thus [it will be]; your Lord says, 'It is easy for Me, and We will make him a sign to the people and a mercy from Us. And it is a matter [already] decreed.' "
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: وَٱلَّتِىٓ أَحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَهَا فَنَفَخْنَا فِيهَا مِن رُّوحِنَا وَجَعَلْنَٰهَا وَٱبْنَهَآ ءَايَةًۭ لِّلْعَٰلَمِينَ
quranVerses.translation: And [mention] the one who guarded her chastity, so We blew into her [garment] through Our angel [Gabriel], and We made her and her son a sign for the worlds.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: وَمَرْيَمَ ٱبْنَتَ عِمْرَٰنَ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَهَا فَنَفَخْنَا فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِنَا وَصَدَّقَتْ بِكَلِمَٰتِ رَبِّهَا وَكُتُبِهِۦ وَكَانَتْ مِنَ ٱلْقَٰنِتِينَ
quranVerses.translation: And [the example of] Mary, the daughter of 'Imran, who guarded her chastity, so We blew into [her garment] through Our angel, and she believed in the words of her Lord and His scriptures and was of the devoutly obedient.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: إِنَّ مَثَلَ عِيسَىٰ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ كَمَثَلِ ءَادَمَ ۖ خَلَقَهُۥ مِن تُرَابٍۢ ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُۥ كُن فَيَكُونُ
quranVerses.translation: Indeed, the example of Jesus to Allah is like that of Adam. He created Him from dust; then He said to him, "Be," and he was.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: قَالَ إِنِّى عَبْدُ ٱللَّهِ ءَاتَىٰنِىَ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَجَعَلَنِى نَبِيًّۭا
quranVerses.translation: [Jesus] said, "Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

bibleVerses.text: Now the birth of Jesus Christ was like this: After his mother, Mary, was engaged to Joseph, before they came together, she was found pregnant by the Holy Spirit. Joseph, her husband, being a righteous man, and not willing to make her a public example, intended to put her away secretly. But when he thought about these things, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying, “Joseph, son of David, don’t be afraid to take to yourself Mary, your wife, for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Spirit. She shall give birth to a son. You shall call his name Jesus, for it is he who shall save his people from their sins.” Now all this has happened, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the Lord through the prophet, saying, “Behold, the virgin shall be with child, and shall give birth to a son. They shall call his name Immanuel”; which is, being interpreted, “God with us.”

Now in the sixth month, the angel Gabriel was sent from God to a city of Galilee, named Nazareth, to a virgin pledged to be married to a man whose name was Joseph, of David’s house. The virgin’s name was Mary. Having come in, the angel said to her, “Rejoice, you highly favored one! The Lord is with you. Blessed are you among women!” But when she saw him, she was greatly troubled at the saying, and considered what kind of salutation this might be. The angel said to her, “Don’t be afraid, Mary, for you have found favor with God. Behold, you will conceive in your womb, and give birth to a son, and will call his name ‘Jesus.’ He will be great, and will be called the Son of the Most High. The Lord God will give him the throne of his father, David, and he will reign over the house of Jacob forever. There will be no end to his Kingdom.” Mary said to the angel, “How can this be, seeing I am a virgin?” The angel answered her, “The Holy Spirit will come on you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. Therefore also the holy one who is born from you will be called the Son of God.
Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign. Behold, the virgin will conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.
